new_findings.title: Auto-resume C2 launchd poller is dead in production: macOS TCC PermissionError crash-loop at the exact moment a marker exists — pending.json unconsumed 9h, zero successful RESUME events ever, failure channel unmonitored
new_findings.evidence: Live 2026-07-02 20:48: /Users/Apple/.claude/auto-resume/launchd.err = 30,618 bytes of 27+ IDENTICAL unhandled tracebacks — `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted: '/Users/Apple/Desktop/Vibe_Code/Bot/AI_Traiding_Bot/llm-wiki/wiki/project/SPRINT_STATE.md'` raised at auto_resume_poll.py:95 (progress_stamp → state.read_bytes()) via main():169; launchctl print gui/…/com.kit.auto-resume → `last exit code = 1`, fresh crash 20:39. ~/.claude/auto-resume/pending.json (ts 11:55, error=rate_limit, session 67b1586c) STILL present 9h later; ~/.claude/auto-resume/log contains ONLY 31 MARKER lines (11:54:05–11:55:03) and zero RESUME/POLL lines ever. Root cause: repo lives under TCC-protected ~/Desktop; /bin/bash+python3 in launchd context (com.kit.auto-resume.plist, StartInterval 600) has no Desktop access — `.exists()` passes, `read_bytes()` EPERMs, exception is UNHANDLED so none of the documented 4 outcomes (RESUMED_PROGRESS/…/STALE-ESCALATE, components/auto-resume.md:20) can ever occur. hooks-selfcheck.sh: 0 mentions of auto-resume/launchd — no guard watches this. Same TCC class independently hit git post-checkout in a worktree (main.log:11973, 'Unable to read current working directory: Operation not permitted').
new_findings.why_weak: The kit's continuity premise ('НЕ отключать хук StopFailure… это контур непрерывности', repo CLAUDE.md) is half-dead: C1 producer fires, C2 consumer crashes precisely when it has work. The research corpus explicitly marked this COVERED with 'infra confirmed live: MARKER … + pending.json written' (log-validation-coverage.json, covered[3]) — it verified the producer and never the consumer. Component page auto-resume.md:31 keeps launchd-C2 as an official optional track post-S67, so the doc claims a capability that has never executed once. Silent fail-comfort violation: the poller is spec'd fail-OPEN but hard-crashes before its own log(), so there is no operator-visible signal at all.
new_findings.proposed_direction: Minimal fix, three parts: (1) wrap progress_stamp()/marker reads in try/except (PermissionError, OSError) → log('TCC-EPERM — нужен Full Disk Access или ручной запуск') + copy marker to stale-tcc-* so the desktop task path still sees it; (2) add a hooks-selfcheck WARN line: launchd.err nonzero growth OR pending.json older than N hours → surface to operator (fits the S69 'WARN-панель' bucket already planned for MEM-02/D3-04); (3) decide the C2 track's fate explicitly: either grant TCC (System Settings → Full Disk Access for /usr/bin/python3 used by the LaunchAgent — document in install.sh status) or retire launchd-C2 and update components/auto-resume.md:20,31 + repo CLAUDE.md Auto-Resume paragraph to desktop-task-only. Add a one-shot install.sh selfcheck: run poller once synchronously and assert it can read SPRINT_STATE.
new_findings.not_duplicate_of: D3-04 (closest auto-resume finding) — that is only about the git mirror of the DESKTOP task prompt lacking a sync gate; it says nothing about the launchd C2 consumer being non-functional. Also distinct from D3-01 (state-backup command grammar) and from log-validation-coverage 'covered[3]', which asserts the opposite (infra live) based on producer-side evidence only.

new_findings.title: Multi-checkout split-brain: desktop-app worktrees + a second full clone carry four parallel SPRINT_STATE truths while every gate resolves state from cwd — stale ACTIVE-phase states persist on disk and a kit fix is stranded on an auto-named claude/* branch
new_findings.evidence: `git worktree list` (live): main repo 5eb5d2f [main] + .claude/worktrees/hardcore-heyrovsky-bc9831 64623fb (detached, mtime Jun 26) + .claude/worktrees/strange-cerf-743771 05efbac [claude/strange-cerf-743771] (mtime Jul 2 18:20 — active today) + /Users/Apple/Desktop/Vibe_Code/Bot/AI_Traiding_Bot_docs 30e60ed [chore/kit-integrate-headroom-ponytail]. Their SPRINT_STATE.md frontmatter SIMULTANEOUSLY: main = sprint 67/between-sprints; hardcore-heyrovsky = sprint 55/phase 4-execution (stale ACTIVE 6 days); _docs = sprint 56/phase 4-execution. Gates read checkout-local truth: phase-advance.sh:55 `repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` → :60 sprint_state_path; review-gate.sh:60-62 same; sprint-flow-check.sh:76 same. Kit fix commit 05efbac ('fix(kit): restore exec bit on cascade-read-check.sh') reachable ONLY from claude/strange-cerf-743771 (git branch --contains), while main holds the identical fix as an UNCOMMITTED mode change (git diff: old mode 100644/new mode 100755) — two heads fixing the same hook without seeing each other. Desktop generates these branches automatically (metadata.json branch 'claude/elastic-noyce-046edb'; main.log: 210 worktree lines).
new_findings.why_weak: Every S58+ enforcement decision is keyed on SPRINT_STATE.phase as 'источник истины' (KIT-002), and S69 D1-01's design gates local `git merge` on 'активная phase 2-8' — but WHICH SPRINT_STATE is consulted depends on the checkout the session runs in. A session in a between-sprints worktree has all sprint gates disarmed while a sprint is active in the main checkout (and vice versa: the S55 4-execution worktree would false-block). Per-task SPRINT_STATE updates, .backup snapshots (state-backup/state-integrity), review-sNN.md artifacts and skill-manifest evidence all fragment across checkouts that nothing reconciles; work committed to claude/* branches is invisible to the manifest and dies with the worktree. The plan's only adjacent item (log-validation-coverage uncovered[2], LOW) treats worktrees as cwd/token FRICTION with 'cd to repo root' hygiene rows — it never touches the state/enforcement split-brain, and no S68-S70 task mentions worktrees.
new_findings.proposed_direction: Small, root-cause-first: (1) in the shared gate helper (or each of the 3 gates + skill-manifest), after repo_root resolution add: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` != `--git-dir` OR repo_root != canonical path constant → treat as worktree/secondary checkout → for BLOCKING gates fail-CLOSED with message 'sprint-гейты валидны только в каноничном checkout /Users/Apple/Desktop/Vibe_Code/Bot/AI_Traiding_Bot — вернись туда или merge ветку worktree'; (2) hooks-selfcheck WARN when `git worktree list` >1 or a sibling *_docs checkout exists with phase != between-sprints (catches the stale-ACTIVE S55/S56 states now on disk); (3) one-time cleanup: merge-or-drop 05efbac и prune hardcore-heyrovsky/_docs. Wire into S69 D1-01 task since its phase-2-8 predicate inherits this hole verbatim.
new_findings.not_duplicate_of: D1-04 (closest) — stale Phase-5 row inside the ONE canonical state file after a crashed session, fixed by M-4 sprint-binding; that fix cannot help here because each checkout's table is internally consistent — there are N whole state FILES, and the gate picks one by cwd. Also distinct from log-validation-coverage uncovered[2] ('worktree/cwd lifecycle friction', LOW token-waste with cd-hygiene fix) and D1-01 (wrong EVENT listened to; this is wrong STATE consulted).

new_findings.title: Third, hallucinated-path agent-memory tree at AI_Traiding_Tool + a standing desktop always-allow for writes to it — wrong-project memory writes are live and now silent
new_findings.evidence: Live filesystem: /Users/Apple/Desktop/Vibe_Code/Bot/AI_Traiding_Tool/.claude/agent-memory/doc-writer/lesson_fsm_intermediate_state_scenario_trap.md exists (dir created Jun 26 23:29 — mid mega-run; the ONLY file in that phantom project root). Desktop metadata.json alwaysAllowedReasons contains: 'Write:Claude requested permissions to edit /Users/Apple/Desktop/Vibe_Code/Bot/AI_Traiding_Tool/.claude/agent-memory/quant-stats-reviewer/memory_kelly_caps.md which is a sensitive file.' — i.e. at least TWO different agents (doc-writer, quant-stats-reviewer) have targeted the typo path, and the permission system has learned a standing allow, so subsequent wrong-path 'sensitive file' writes no longer prompt. The typo class is documented in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md §9b only as a READ hazard ('AI_Traiding_Bot vs AI_Traiding_Tool'); no write-side guard exists.
new_findings.why_weak: Memory shards written there are invisible to every consumer: not in .claude/agent-memory (harness-loaded), not in ~/.claude/agent-memory (the D2-01 second tree), not indexed, not in git — the lesson is silently lost, and the S70 D2-01 fix (repoint 3 doc-agent prompts between the two KNOWN trees) neither detects nor prevents a third tree because the root cause is path hallucination at write time, not a hardcoded prompt path. The always-allow entry converts a one-off hallucination into a permanent quiet failure mode for any agent that mistypes the project root on a Write.
new_findings.proposed_direction: Tiny: (1) delete/merge the orphan shard into the canonical doc-writer memory and remove the AI_Traiding_Tool tree; (2) add one hooks-selfcheck WARN line: `ls -d /Users/Apple/Desktop/Vibe_Code/Bot/AI_Traiding_* | grep -v "_Bot$\|_Bot_docs$"` non-empty → 'phantom project dir (path-typo write) — разбери и удали'; (3) fold into the S70 agent-memory lifecycle task (D2-04+MEM-05) as an extra check in the planned orphan-memory WARN; (4) operator: purge the AI_Traiding_Tool always-allow entries from desktop session permissions so wrong-path sensitive writes prompt again.
new_findings.not_duplicate_of: D2-01 (closest) — split-brain between the two DESIGNED trees (~/.claude vs .claude) caused by hardcoded prompt paths, fixed by repointing three named prompt lines; this finding is a third UNDESIGNED tree created by path hallucination plus a permission-system allow that makes recurrence silent — neither mechanism nor fix overlaps. Also not MEM-05/D2-04 (index/budget hygiene of memories in the correct trees).

new_findings.title: The 2.5-month mega-run desktop session ran with permissionMode=bypassPermissions (+ chrome skip_all_permission_checks), and the research corpus recommends extending bypassPermissions to scheduled tasks — leaving self-editable kit hooks as the ONLY enforcement layer on a real-money repo
new_findings.evidence: metadata.json (session-export): "permissionMode":"bypassPermissions", "chromePermissionMode":"skip_all_permission_checks", createdAt=1776618119205 (2026-04-20) → lastActivityAt=2026-07-01, completedTurns=618, writtenBranches=[…,"main",…] — the whole S47-S67 mega-run window. The 17 alwaysAllowedReasons entries (writes to ~/.claude/hooks/*.sh, ~/.claude/agents/*.md, ~/.claude/settings.json) show the harness's sensitive-file prompting existed earlier and was progressively disabled, then superseded by full bypass. Meanwhile log-validation-coverage.json uncovered[3] proposes for unattended runs: 'pre-approve an allowlist (or bypassPermissions in the Scheduled Task) so a permission prompt can never stall an unattended session' — normalizing bypass as the fix. Under bypass, the only remaining barriers are the kit PreToolUse hooks, which (a) the gated session itself can rewrite (~/.claude/hooks/*.sh writes don't prompt; hooks-selfcheck's bash -n checks syntax, not intent), and (b) are documented by S59-S62 as forgeable/bypassable at the accepted boundary.
new_findings.why_weak: Defense went from two independent layers (harness permissions + kit hooks) to one layer that is writable by the entity it polices — for a repo whose backlog says money paths are approaching live trading. Nobody in the 47 findings examined the permission-mode dimension at all (the corpus discusses hooks, skills, memory, tokens — never permissionMode), and the only place it surfaces, it is being recommended as a convenience fix without noting the single-layer consequence. This is an operator-policy weak spot, not a code bug — hence MEDIUM, prerequisite = compromised/hallucinating session, which is precisely the S61 threat model the kit already takes seriously.
new_findings.proposed_direction: Do not ship bypassPermissions into the S67 Scheduled Task (amend log-validation-coverage uncovered[3]'s proposal): use permissions.allow allowlist + acceptEdits instead, so unattended runs can't stall yet still prompt-or-deny on ~/.claude/hooks/**, ~/.claude/settings.json and kit/hooks/** writes. Probe whether permissions.deny rules remain enforced under bypassPermissions in the current Claude Code build (10-min test); if yes, add deny entries for hook/settings self-modification as the cheap second layer; if no, record an explicit operator decision (like S64 WARN) that autonomous sprints accept single-layer enforcement, so the boundary is documented rather than accidental.
new_findings.not_duplicate_of: D1-03 / S61 self-skip and forgery findings (closest in spirit) — those analyze bypasses WITHIN the hook layer assuming hooks are the boundary; this finding is about the layer ABOVE hooks being switched off globally for 2.5 months (and about to be codified for scheduled tasks), which no confirmed finding, panel verdict, or S68-S70 task mentions. Also distinct from log-validation-coverage uncovered[3], which flags permission STALLS and proposes the opposite direction.
